publication_finding: The 2019 KPHC publication describes population and household tables for county, sub-county and administrative units (county, sub-county, division, location and sub-location). It does not publish a direct table for the current 290 constituencies. KNBS's constituency table published in 2013 is based on the earlier census/boundary configuration and cannot be assigned to the current 2012-01 290-constituency registry without an authoritative crosswalk.
rules: Do not inherit a sub-county value into a constituency merely because a name overlaps.
Do not aggregate administrative units to constituencies without an authoritative 2019 administrative-unit to 2012-01 constituency crosswalk.
Do not remap the legacy pre-2012 KNBS constituency table to the current 290 constituencies.
A census questionnaire field recording constituency does not by itself constitute a published constituency statistic.
Refresh this closure if KNBS publishes a direct 290-constituency table or an authoritative crosswalk supporting deterministic aggregation.

decisions.source: KNBS — 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census Reports
decisions.reason: KNBS's 2019 KPHC publication does not publish population as a direct current-290-constituency table. Published county/sub-county/administrative-unit values are not inherited or cross-walked without an authoritative boundary mapping; the older KNBS constituency table predates the current 2012-01 constituency configuration.
decisions.refresh_trigger: KNBS publishes a direct current-290 constituency population table or an authoritative 2019 administrative-unit to 2012-01 constituency crosswalk.

decisions.source: KNBS — 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census Reports
decisions.reason: KNBS's 2019 KPHC publication does not publish average household size as a direct current-290-constituency table. County/sub-county values are not inherited, and lower administrative-unit household counts are not aggregated without an authoritative constituency crosswalk; the older KNBS constituency table predates the current 2012-01 constituency configuration. P28A re-audit (2026-09-16) independently re-verified this by downloading and text-extracting KNBS 2019 KPHC Volume II (Distribution of Population by Administrative Units, https://www.knbs.or.ke/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/2019-Kenya-population-and-Housing-Census-Volume-2-Distribution-of-Population-by-Administrative-Units.pdf) in full: its own List of Tables shows Table 2.4 (Distribution of Population by Sex, Number of Households, Land Area, Population Density and Sub Locations) is the finest administrative tier published -- there is no Table 2.x for constituencies. 'Constituency' and 'Ward' appear in Volume II exactly twice, both times as fields on the raw household enumeration questionnaire reproduced in the appendix, not as a published aggregate table -- a census questionnaire field recording constituency does not by itself constitute a published constituency statistic (see rules, above). The re-audit also confirmed KNBS administrative sub-counties (the finest county-nested tier that is aggregated, in Table 2.3) are not the same delineation as the 290 IEBC electoral constituencies and cannot substitute for them without a crosswalk KNBS has not published: e.g. Table 1.2 lists 5 KNBS sub-counties for Kwale County (Kinango, Lunga Lunga, Matuga, Msambweni, Samburu) against Kwale's 4 IEBC constituencies, and 11 KNBS sub-counties for Meru County against Meru's 9 IEBC constituencies. Separately, the re-audit downloaded and text-extracted the older, standalone 'Constituency Population by Sex, Number of Households, Area and Density' publication (https://www.knbs.or.ke/constituency-population-by-sex-number-of-households-area-and-density/, republished 2013) and confirmed it is 2009-census Volume 1B (Population Distribution by Political Units), whose own text states its tables 'are tabulated for the 210 constituencies and the 47 counties in Kenya' -- i.e. it is definitively the pre-2012-delimitation constituency configuration referenced above, not a current-290 table, and using it to derive household size (population / households) would require exactly the unavailable 210-to-290 crosswalk this closure already prohibits inventing. The re-audit also checked the KNBS Kenya National Data Archive (NADA) catalog entry for the 2019 KPHC (https://statistics.knbs.or.ke/nada/index.php/catalog/116); its public study metadata documents no constituency-level geographic identifier or downloadable constituency aggregate and describes geographic coverage only at 'The Whole Country' / household-and-individual microdata level, not a released constituency tabulation. No credible S0-S4 primary or secondary source, and no defensible S1 official-derived computation (an authoritative population figure and an authoritative household-count figure at the same current-290-constituency granularity), was found. As of this re-audit, IEBC has also publicly ruled out any constituency/ward boundary delimitation review before the 2027 general election -- the constitutional March 2024 deadline was missed, and a January 2025 High Court ruling (under appeal) invalidated the underlying 2019 census population figures for Garissa, Wajir and Mandera counties specifically -- so the current 2012-01, 290-constituency boundary remains the operative geography with no imminent republication of constituency-level census tables or a fresh KNBS-IEBC crosswalk in prospect.
decisions.refresh_trigger: KNBS publishes a direct current-290 constituency household-size table (population and household counts both tabulated at current-constituency granularity), or an authoritative 2019 administrative-unit (or 2009-to-2012 delimitation) to 2012-01 constituency crosswalk that KNBS or IEBC has certified as exact and complete.
